items.prompt:
Read both passages below.

Passage 1: Sam likes to eat apples. He has one every day after school.

Passage 2: Lily likes to eat bananas. She has one every day after school.

What is one way Sam and Lily are the SAME?
items.answer: Sam and Lily are both the same because they each eat a piece of fruit every day after school.

steps: Read both passages.
Look for something both Sam and Lily do. Both eat a fruit every day after school.
That is what they share: eating a fruit after school each day.

items.prompt:
Read both passages below.

Passage 1: Ben has a dog. His dog is big and brown. Ben walks his dog every morning.

Passage 2: Rosa has a cat. Her cat is small and white. Rosa plays with her cat every morning.

What is one way Ben and Rosa are DIFFERENT?
items.answer: Ben and Rosa are different because Ben has a dog and Rosa has a cat. Also, Ben walks his pet and Rosa plays with hers.

steps: Look for things that are not the same.
Ben has a dog; Rosa has a cat. That is different.
Ben walks his pet; Rosa plays with hers. That is also different.

items.prompt:
Read both passages below.

Passage 1: Jade went to the park. She played on the swings.

Passage 2: Miles went to the park. He played on the slide.

What is the same about Jade and Miles? What is different?
items.answer: Jade and Miles are the same because they both went to the park. They are different because Jade played on the swings and Miles played on the slide.

steps: Same: Both Jade and Miles went to the park.
Different: Jade played on swings; Miles played on the slide.
They were in the same place but did different activities.

items.prompt:
Read both passages below.

Passage 1: Frog jumps into the pond to get cool. He loves the cold water.

Passage 2: Turtle walks into the pond to get cool. She loves the cold water.

How are Frog and Turtle the same? How are they different?
items.answer: Frog and Turtle are the same because they both go into the pond to cool down and both love the cold water. They are different because Frog jumps in and Turtle walks in.

steps: Same: Both go to the pond to cool off and both love cold water.
Different: Frog jumps in; Turtle walks in.
Same goal, different way of getting there.

How are Tim and Ann the same? How are they different?
items.answer: Tim and Ann are the same because they are both scared of thunder. They are different because Tim hides under his bed and Ann holds her mom's hand.

steps: Same: Both are scared of thunder.
Different: Tim hides under the bed; Ann holds her mom's hand.
They feel the same fear but respond in different ways.

Both of them ate the bug quickly.

items.prompt:
Read both passages below.

Passage 1: The lion roars when he is hungry. All the animals in the field run away.

Passage 2: The lion growls when he is happy. All the animals in the field run away.

What is the same in both passages? What is different?
items.answer: What is the same is that in both passages, the lion makes a loud noise and all the animals run away. What is different is why the lion makes the noise: in the first he is hungry, and in the second he is happy.

steps: Same: The lion makes a noise and the animals run away in both passages.
Different: The reason for the noise is different. First passage: hungry. Second passage: happy.
Same reaction from the animals, but different reasons for the lion's sound.

items.answer: Maria and Carlos are the same because they both always do the same activity at recess and both are very good at what they do. They are different because Maria plays jump rope and Carlos plays soccer.

Different: Maria plays jump rope; Carlos plays soccer.
Same dedication, different sports.

items.answer: Dana and Ivan are the same because they both went to school. They are different because Dana woke up early and ate breakfast, while Ivan woke up late and had no breakfast.

Different: Dana woke up early and ate; Ivan woke up late and did not eat.
Same destination, very different mornings.

items.prompt:
Read both passages below.

Passage 2: The puppy chewed on a toy inside the house. She wagged her tail the whole time.

What is the same about the puppy in both passages? What is different?
items.answer: What is the same is that in both passages the puppy chews on something and wags her tail. What is different is where she is (yard vs. inside) and what she chews (a stick vs. a toy).

steps: Same: The puppy is chewing something and wagging her tail in both passages.
Different: First, she is in the yard with a stick. Second, she is inside with a toy.
Same happy behavior, different places and objects.

items.answer: Keiko and Marco are the same because they both felt excited on the first day of first grade. They are different because Keiko talked to someone right away while Marco sat quietly and waited for others to speak to him first.

Different: Keiko started conversations; Marco waited for others to come to him.
Same feeling, different ways of responding to that feeling.
